ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Pablo Neruda — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Two-week review with the medical oncology consultation the same day: biopsy and staging results, the diagnosis, shared decision on treatment, the start of apalutamide, genetic testing, and bone density

text.paragraph: Two-week review: biopsy and staging results; medical oncology seen today. [S]

Mr. Neruda returns two weeks after his first visit, with a professional Spanish interpreter. In the past ten days he had an MRI of the prostate, a targeted biopsy at the urology practice, a CT scan, a bone scan and a PSMA PET/CT. The results were explained to him this morning by Dr. Okonkwo-Lund of medical oncology and again today: prostate cancer, Gleason 4+4, that has spread to two lymph nodes in the pelvis and to two places in the bones, the right hip bone and the lowest lumbar vertebra, with nothing in the lungs, liver or other organs. He chose, after hearing the options, to start apalutamide today, with a leuprolide injection in one week and radiotherapy to the prostate in about six weeks. His blood was drawn today for germline genetic testing after counseling. He had his bone density scan this morning. The right hip pain is a little better on acetaminophen, 5 of 10 at worst, and still wakes him some nights; he has no leg weakness, numbness, or change in bladder or bowel control. His urinary symptoms are unchanged. He feels the news is hard but says he would rather know. He wants to keep writing every morning and to continue his duties. [S]

list.item:
Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, Grade Group 4, cT3a N1 M1b, low volume (C61). De novo metastatic disease, low volume on conventional imaging (two bone metastases, both in the spine and pelvis, and no visceral disease), confirmed by PSMA PET/CT. The plan follows the consultation today: androgen deprivation with an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor, plus radiotherapy to the prostate for low-volume disease. Docetaxel is not added, because its survival benefit is in high-volume disease. [S]
Apalutamide 240 mg once daily from today.
Leuprolide 22.5 mg in one week at the oncology clinic, then every twelve weeks; apalutamide started a week before covers the testosterone flare.
Radiotherapy to the prostate, 55 Gy in 20 fractions, about six weeks after starting.
Germline testing sent today; somatic testing of the biopsy tissue requested.

Bone metastases (right ilium, L5) (C79.51). Pain improving on acetaminophen; no signs of spinal cord compression. Androgen deprivation usually eases bone pain within weeks. [S]
Acetaminophen 1000 mg up to three times a day.
Warning signs of cord compression reviewed again in Spanish, with a written card.

Low bone mass before androgen deprivation (M85.89). Femoral neck T-score -2.1 and L1 to L4 -1.4. FRAX, counting androgen deprivation as a cause of secondary osteoporosis, gives a ten-year hip fracture risk of 3.4 percent and a major osteoporotic fracture risk of 13 percent; the hip risk is above the 3 percent threshold for a bone-protective drug. [S]
Dental examination before denosumab.
Denosumab 60 mg every six months, the osteoporosis dose, once calcium is confirmed normal and vitamin D is being replaced.
Calcium 1000 to 1200 mg a day from food; walking and resistance exercise.

Vitamin D insufficiency (E55.9). 25-hydroxyvitamin D 22 ng/mL. [S]
Cholecalciferol 1945 units daily from today; recheck in four weeks before denosumab.

Hypertension (I10). 142/86 mm Hg, above goal. Apalutamide is a strong CYP3A4 inducer and is expected to lower amlodipine levels. [S]
Blood pressure at the four-week visit; amlodipine dose to be adjusted then.
